evidence_summary: When combined with NODE_PRE summaries, adding local, meso, or far relation pools yields negligible held-out gain (<0.5 pp, with all 95% CIs bounding or touching zero). Isolated REL_LOCAL and REL_FAR linear probes achieve nearly identical performance (~33-34% accuracy), and combination adds virtually nothing on held-out test splits.

Falsified by linear probe diagnostics. Adding pairwise relation content descriptors to node summaries produces delta accuracy within [-0.005, +0.005] on both Public and Private splits, with 95% bootstrap CIs firmly containing zero across v1, v2, and v2.1. Furthermore, symmetric relation descriptors perform identically to directed descriptors.

Strong empirical support. Attention entropy reveals that each node effectively attends to only ~11-16 of its 48 neighbors across all layers (top-8 neighbors capture >80% of attention mass). In functional replay, removing all local edges (NO_LOCAL) drops accuracy by only ~1.2-1.6 pp, and restricting connectivity to local+meso (NO_FAR, removing 1,032 far edges) retains 66.7% accuracy with 0.917 readout cosine similarity. A structured sparse topology is well motivated.

Strong empirical support. Replacing sample-specific dynamic attention weights with the static Train-derived mean attention template causes a severe, catastrophic drop of over 9.3 percentage points on PrivateTest (accuracy collapses from 69.94% to 60.60%, and macro-F1 drops by 12.4 pp). Instance-dependent attention routing is essential for expression recognition.

Per pre-registered protocol, H5 is gated on H2. Because pairwise relational content failed to provide held-out gain beyond node summaries (H2 DEPRIORITIZED), H5 remains strictly closed. Hypergraph and complex higher-order relation modeling are not justified for FER2013.
